answer: One way to keep fake agents out is to make each identity pay a real cost before it can act. A new agent could be required to stake a small deposit and pass a proof of unique hardware through a kernel level attestation, so spinning up thousands of copies stops being free. A bridge that links identities across networks would then check that attestation instead of trusting a username, and a single operator trying to cross the canyon between separate reputation systems with cloned accounts would hit the same stake each time.
